rows.reason: Line 6 (running onto 7) has the tench fade into deep water and line 8 quotes 'if you had run quick!' verbatim; the script ties the fish leaving to Bevis blaming Mark's delay, which is the key.
Lines 10-11 and 12-13 are correctly described: same elephant example with the shooter and the gun-hander swapped; matches the key.
Lines 38-39 (nails plan), 39-40 (Mark far ahead) and 40-41 (boast he explored the new sea first) are all on the cited lines; walks clearly to the key.

Doesn't teach the link to the key. It quotes 'must not stay in such a place' (line 72) but stops before 'where he might lose his balance' (line 73), the only words that show he could fall. No sentence connects that reminder to ignoring the dragonfly, so a child is not shown why the key ('reminded that he could fall') is right.
Line 17 (rushing to stop Tinette, taken hold of) and lines 19-20 (hand kept on her to prevent her running forward) are accurate and lead to the key.

The line 29 quotation 'yours would have been hard and stale by then' is verbatim, and 'by then' is correctly read as 'by the time she goes home' (line 28). Separates the key from the 'stale by now' minimal pair.
Line 33 ('to make sure that she could depend upon it') and line 34 ('quite as many') are accurate; shows the repetition is checking the promise.

Child-facing form: the last sentence, 'A thing that goes on a head, and it is hers.', is a fragment with no main clause for its first half. It also asserts the hidden thing is worn on the head, which lines 39-41 do not say; the hat only appears at line 42. It also credits the meaning to 'his little nods' alone, where line 41 gives it to the signs and nods together.
Line 11 (Ralph agrees), line 12 (round it ten times more quickly) and line 13 (the result, not the reason) are accurate; separates the cause from the thief-search distractors.
Stuart's list is on lines 21-22 and Fogg's two-word answer is on line 23; correctly concludes the eighty days already allow for those delays.
Line 39 ('let's go on with the game'), line 41 (takes up the pack, puts it down) and line 42 (will wager the four thousand) are accurate and in order; shows the change of mind.
Line 56, lines 57-58 and lines 59-60 are accurate; 80 days = 1,920 hours = 115,200 minutes checks out; leads to the key.
Lines 14-15 ('spend the whole game' / 'running at the back of somebody's head') are on the cited lines; line 12 correctly set aside as his own end.
Line 23 ('let in on purpose'), line 26 ('could have had it') and lines 26-27 ('hands on it') are accurate and together give the key.

Doesn't teach the half of the key the question turns on, 'although his end has none'. It never points to line 33 ('two jumpers and the air between them'), and it never points to the contrast in 'still' on line 34. Lines 36-37, 'nobody has ever said there is not one', are reported without showing that there really is no net.
Line 28 (more things to find out in this house) and line 29 (will certainly stay and find out) are accurate; line 25 correctly set aside as the meat.
'licked his lips' (line 44), 'splendid hunting-ground' (line 44) and the tail growing bottle-brushy (lines 44-45) are accurate; leads to the key.
Line 55 (cowered without answering), line 56 (hiss from the grass at the foot of the bush) and line 58 (Nag, the big black cobra) are accurate; shows the snake below the nest.

Wrong line cited. 'Line 65 says look, and be afraid' is wrong, because 'Look, and be' is on line 64 and line 65 holds only 'afraid!'. Also, 'Line 64 tells the story of the mark' is only partly right: the story begins on line 63 ('The great God Brahm put his mark upon all our people').
Line 12 (nobody to open the net; said on Monday), line 13 (still asleep then) and line 14 ('the instruction is basically out of date') are accurate; gives the key.
Line 23 ('he knows what they are, which proves') runs onto line 24 ('they were ready') and is cited at the start line. Line 21 is correctly set aside. Shows what Dilan takes as proof.
Line 32 (would rather not say), line 33 (office has a window) and line 34 (open all afternoon) are accurate; points the child to the evidence for the open-window inference without stating it first.

Misleads. 'Line 38 has Mrs Farrell say the word again.' leaves 'again' unquoted, so it reads as 'says the word a second time' rather than naming the word in the stem. The word itself is on line 39, not line 38. The script also never reaches line 40, 'everybody has moved on from it', which supports 'which he thinks is finished'.
Line 22 (told Jo she would make her pay for being so cross, 'and I have') is accurate; line 19 correctly set aside; supports the key.

Doesn't teach the 'holds it in' half of the key and risks misleading. The first sentence, 'wanted to lay her head down and cry' (line 39), is the literal-lookalike distractor, and the script never says that she did not cry. 'she winked hard' (line 41) is left unexplained as holding back tears. Lines 40-41 ('tears were an unmanly weakness', 'couldn't quite forgive yet') are skipped.
Line 53 (go after them), lines 53-54 (till Jo has got good-natured with Laurie), line 54 (take a quiet minute) and line 55 (friends again) are accurate and in order; the key comes after the evidence.
'Staked late' (line 7), 'taller than me and him put together' and 'did not say so' (line 8), and 'not that kind of conversation' (line 9) are all accurate; leads to the key.
Line 23 ('counted them into the bucket out loud', 'lost his place twice') and line 24 ('from where he thought he had got to') are accurate; shows he cannot keep track.
Line 32 (garlic in November), line 33 (her up here to do the string for him) and lines 30-31 (Alan takes the plot from the autumn) are accurate; correctly draws out the assumption.
Line 38 (Mum driving him Thursday; 'it was nothing') and line 39 (turns to the parking price) are accurate; shows him playing it down.
Lines 19-20 ('glad that he had been spared'), line 20 ('a man of quick temper', paraphrased correctly) and line 21 ('not have taken it so placidly') are accurate; leads to the key.

Doesn't teach the key. 'as a man looks who thinks on flight' (line 54) is the only words that support 'looking for a way out', and the script never explains that 'flight' here means running away. The other evidence it lists, the step trembling and the hand shaking, fits the 'he is ill' distractor just as well, so the script does not separate the key from it.
Line 9 (what Mum said) and line 10 ('Your mum says a lot of things') are accurate, and line 10 has the bolt work go on. Shows him brushing her words aside.
Line 31 (not going to lift it), line 32 (her mother has him down as about ninety) and lines 32-33 (the knock 'is his joke') are accurate; supports making light of being thought too old.
Line 35 (more out than ever seen), lines 35-36 (not going anywhere in particular) and line 36 (same square of air) are accurate; gives the key.

Leaves out the evidence for the key. The key is 'Something he heard', and it rests on line 45 'He is listening to the door' and line 46 'Oh, hang on'. The script stops at 'then he stops' and never mentions listening. Its only evidence is something passing his ear and him swatting at it, which points the child towards the swatting distractor instead.
